thread:
Maya P: evening pass — TL;DR: brief spike in /v1/generate p95 around midday due to an unintended cache eviction during a deployment. Customers saw elevated latency (mostly 1–2s extra p95) and a small number of 502s for requests routed to the freshly-started workers. Pager triggered + mitigations applied. Current status: stabilized, autoscaler scaled up, fallback route enabled. Next steps listed below.

OpsBot: INCIDENT: HIGH_LATENCY /v1/generate p95 > 1200ms (region: us-west-2) — triggered 2408121200 — incident id INC-2408-77 — severity: P2 — paging oncall.

Liam K: got the page, jumping in. Quick check — metrics show a KV cache regen spike and many cold kv-miss fills after the deployment that started at ~11:45. Batcher queue also briefly backed up.

Alex R: I rolled the deployment back at 12:10 to the previous canary. That reduced the eviction rate. I also temporarily disabled the aggressive prefetch flag in the model runtime config.

Rachel S: Verified customer impact via apm traces — most affected were multi-shot chat sessions with long contexts (>=1024 tokens). Single-turn shorter calls unaffected. I filed a short customer-impact note in INC-2408-77.

Maya P: actions taken so far:
- rollback to canary v2.3.1 (Alex)
- scaled embedding/llm pool by +20% (autoscaler override) — temporary until kv warm-up finishes
- enabled fallback routing to rwd-llm-small for non-critical routes to keep tail latency under SLO
- runbook link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/kv-eviction (see section "eviction-regressions")

Liam K: quick verification commands I ran:```bash
# check p95 by route
curl -s 'https://metrics.internal/api/query?metric=p95&route=/v1/generate&region=us-west-2'
# check kv eviction rate
kubectl -n infer logs -l app=kv-cache | grep eviction | tail -n 30
```

OpsBot: Note: alert resolved at 2408122100 (auto). Recommended follow-up: post-incident eval and check warm-up window.

Alex R: Current status: CPU/GPU utilization back to baseline, KV miss rate trending down but still ~15% above baseline. Warm-up should finish in next 20–30m. I've pinned the canary to previous version for now.

Rachel S: Customer calls: I reached out to two customers who were hit the hardest (enterprise accounts) and offered status updates. No escalations yet. Documented messages in the customer tracker.

Maya P: coverage for tonight — primary: Liam K (til 03:30 UTC), secondary: Alex R (til 03:30 UTC). Morning handoff (03:30 UTC): Rachel S will take primary; Maya will be secondary. Oncall Rotation Bot: please update calendar.

Oncall Rotation Bot: Updated rotation: Liam K set as primary for 2408-12 19:00-03:30 UTC, Alex R secondary. Reminder: mark yourself "on-call" in the console.

Liam K: quick checklist for whoever picks this up next:
- confirm kv miss rate gets back to <5% above baseline
- if misses persist, increase pool size or temporarily enable persistent KV warmers (runbook step 4)
- watch p95 /v1/generate and p99 for related routes
- if 502s reappear, flip fallback routing to local small-models and open a support note for affected customers

Maya P: outstanding action items before handoff:
- Alex: keep the canary pinned and monitor deployment pipeline for retries (assigned)
- Rachel: finish drafting the incident impact note and add to INC-2408-77 (assigned)
- Liam: let ops-bot know when kv miss rate drops under threshold so we can close the incident formally (assigned)

Alex R: noted. I'll leave a proc snippet here in case someone needs to manually re-enable fallback routing:```yaml
# flip fallback: set route_priority for /v1/generate
routes:
  - name: generate
    priority: [rwd-llm-small, rwd-llm-large]
```

Rachel S: adding a short customer-facing blurb for the tracker: "We observed transient elevated latency for certain long-context requests due to a cache warm-up after a deployment. We rolled back the change, scaled capacity temporarily, and fallbacks were enabled to preserve performance. We're monitoring and will follow up with a full RCA."

Liam K: I'm going to stay on the incident for the next 30m and will post any updates. If you get paged, follow the runbook and ping me.

Maya P: thanks all. Post-incident follow-up: schedule RCA meeting tomorrow 16:00 PST, invite owners (Alex, Liam, Rachel, infra-ml). I'll create the calendar invite and a short postmortem stub.

OpsBot: Reminder: runbook link pinned in thread. Incident INC-2408-77 moved to "stabilized" mode.

Liam K: :thumbsup: closing note for now — leaving logs and traces in the incident ticket. If anything flares up I will wake up the channel.

Maya P: handoff complete. Good night. :coffee:
